cues.say: Component seven: sweeper and reconciliation jobs.
These are small programs that run on a timer and clean up. A sweeper releases things that got stuck. A reconciliation job compares your records with an outside source, and fixes any gaps.
Like closing time at a shop, when you count the till against the receipts. Running a program on a schedule is classically called cron.
Why do you need them? At the pizza shop, checkout puts a hold on the pizzas, then sends the customer to Stripe's payment page.
Fifty customers abandon that page. Their pizzas stay held, and nobody else can buy them.
Worse, one customer pays, but Stripe's webhook, the message that says paid, never arrives. That order is never cooked.
The sweeper runs every minute, and finds the holds that have expired.
Before releasing one, it asks Stripe: was this paid? If not, the pizzas go back on sale. If it was, the order goes to the kitchen. That catches the lost webhook.
Reconciliation is the nightly safety net. It lists Stripe's payments, and compares them with your orders, one by one.
Here's a payment with no matching paid order. The job marks the order paid, so nothing is left hanging.
You use them for expired holds, on stock, seats or bookings,
for stuck orders, like one that's been sending for an hour,
and for matching payments against an outside record.
Now the real case. Kickoff night: fifty customers abandon the Stripe page, and one paid order's webhook is lost.
Without these jobs, those pizzas stay held all night, and the paying customer never gets dinner.
With them, within a minute of the holds expiring, all fifty carts are released and back on sale, and the paid order reaches the kitchen.
Here's where it sits: off to the side, on a timer. The jobs read the database and ask Stripe, but no customer ever waits on them.
Two things to know. Run one copy of each job at a time, so two sweepers don't fight over the same hold.
And make every fix safe to repeat. If a job dies halfway, the next run simply does it again.
In the interview, say: every minute, release expired holds, after asking Stripe whether they were paid.
